vulnerability.impact: SOCKS5 heap buffer overflow during hostname resolution

entry_points: do_SOCKS5 / Curl_SOCKS5 (lib/socks.c, SOCKS5 handshake; lines ~548-671) - hostname length is not validated before sending/processing when remote name resolution (SOCKS5h) is requested
ground_truth.fix_commit: fb4415d8aee6c1045be932a34fe6107c2f5ed147 (socks: return error if hostname too long for remote resolve), included in curl 8.4.0 (ancestor of curl-8_4_0). Pinned snapshot 6fa1d817e5b1a00d7d0c8168091877476b499317 equals the curl-8_3_0 tag commit.
ground_truth.affected_range: curl 7.69.0 through 8.3.0 (fixed in 8.4.0) when built with SOCKS5 support and a proxy with remote name resolution; exploitability requires HTTP proxy or SOCKS5 proxy configured.
ground_truth.finding_match_rule: TP: report localizes the SOCKS5 handshake buffer sizing/hostname handling in lib/socks.c (Curl_SOCKS5/do_SOCKS5 path with remote resolve), names CVE-2023-38545, and attributes heap buffer overflow / possible RCE. A generic proxy or DNS finding is not TP.
ground_truth.safe_reproduction_predicate: Static predicate: 8.3.0 socks.c writes up to 255-byte hostname into a 255-byte buffer without the length rejection added by fb4415d8. Dynamic reproduction: run the snapshot curl against a local SOCKS5 test proxy, send a >255-byte hostname, and observe curl exit/behavior under ASAN; no external network and no files written.
